clue.text: Groom at war

blocks.note: to groom hair is to comb it
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bridegroom away fighting in a war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' reads as a bridegroom, but here it is the verb for tidying hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Combat is armed fighting between forces, a close synonym for warfare.

clue.text: Hood for animal novice

blocks.note: a cow is a farm animal
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A protective hood made for a young or inexperienced animal.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L plate, so L stands for any novice.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowl is the loose hood worn by monks, attached to their habit.

clue.text: Wet way one goes in, mainly

definitions.note: the answer is an adverb meaning in a wet way

indicators.note: something that goes in is placed inside another word

blocks.note: mainly means for the most part
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A description of how someone mostly enters a damp place.
explanation.walkthrough: The single letter slots into the word for mainly, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb describes doing something with dampness, which is acting in a wet manner.

clue.text: Never-present style of wool-gatherer

blocks.note: surface reading: the habits of someone who collects fleece but never turns up
setter's reading: the manner of a daydreamer, whose mind is never present

explanation.surface: Someone gathering wool from sheep who never seems to be around.
explanation.walkthrough: Wool-gathering is an idiom for daydreaming, so the wool-gatherer is a dreamer whose mind is elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things absently means acting with attention elsewhere, the typical manner of an inattentive daydreamer.

clue.text: Room to mature in modern times

definitions.note: the answer is a noun phrase for the modern era, or an adjective for it

blocks.note: room means space
to age is to mature, like wine

explanation.surface: Somewhere spacious enough to grow up in the present day.
explanation.definitionFit: The space age is the era of space exploration, a byword for contemporary times and technology.

clue.text: Dire prognosis for failing sentry

blocks.note: first meaning: an unpromising outlook for the future
second meaning: a guard who is bad at keeping watch

explanation.surface: A grim forecast for a guard who is not doing the job well.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for unpromising prospects, and also literally describes an incompetent watchman.

clue.text: Attractive saint, the most appealing

blocks.note: attractive means cute
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A handsome saint who is the most charming of all.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutest is the superlative of cute, meaning most charming or endearing.

clue.text: Pleasant, but am I clever?

blocks.note: taken as written
clever means able

explanation.surface: Someone who is agreeable but wonders whether they are bright enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a question, the clue becomes 'am I able?', run together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable describes a friendly, good-natured person, so it matches pleasant in manner.

clue.text: Salute the hoped-for sight test result

blocks.note: first meaning: the parade-ground command to turn the head in salute
second meaning: vision checked and found correct

explanation.surface: Saluting the good outcome of an eye examination.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command directs soldiers to turn their heads as a mark of respect; jokingly, it also means healthy vision.

clue.text: Why one manuscript adapted a fanciful idea

indicators.note: adapted means altered into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript

explanation.surface: A writer asks why a single manuscript was turned into a flight of fancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Whimsy is playfully quaint or fanciful humour, or a sudden capricious notion.

clue.text: Drink for the team on the left ...

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Buying drinks for the team, linked by the ellipsis to the sober folk of the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, port side is the left-hand side when facing forward.

clue.text: ... but no drink for those who prefer to be this!

definitions.text: no drink for those who prefer to be this

blocks.clueFragment: but no drink for those who prefer to be this
blocks.note: surface reading: following the previous clue, teetotallers refusing the round

blocks.clueFragment: those who prefer to be this
blocks.note: setter's reading: the state of being completely free of alcohol

explanation.surface: Teetotallers turning down a drink while the team has port.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for being completely and utterly free of any alcoholic intoxication.

clue.text: Phoning ace, for example, to get a visiting token in America

blocks.note: phoning someone is calling them
an ace is an example of a playing card

explanation.surface: Telephoning someone with an ace of a ticket to visit the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans say calling card for what Britons call a visiting card, left when paying a social visit.

clue.text: Organised all broody circle in the highest rank

indicators.note: organised means put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: Sitting hens in a circle are arranged by social rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal blood means descent from a royal family, the top tier of hereditary social standing.

clue.text: Repay bruiser -- me? Unfortunately!

indicators.note: something that goes unfortunately goes wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried person asks if they must pay back a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: To reimburse someone is to pay back money they have spent or lost.

clue.text: Right to go in to plead for Titanic''s fate

indicators.note: the first item is told to go into the word that follows

blocks.note: to plead is to beg
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A plea to do right, set against the sinking of the great liner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Titanic sank in 1912 after striking an iceberg, here shortened to its final four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A berg, short for iceberg, was the floating mass of ice that sank the liner.

clue.text: Near the late Bernard Shaw -- wow!

blocks.note: by means near, as in 'stand by me'
the playwright's full name was George Bernard Shaw

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in amazement at being close to the dead playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, used just like an astonished interjection.

clue.text: Old Indian at home with accountant

blocks.note: someone at home is in
CA is chartered accountant

explanation.surface: An elderly man from India relaxing indoors with his accountant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Indian' suggests someone from India; it means a native of South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca were an indigenous people of Peru whose empire fell to Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Talked of that eccentric captured by around December

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are jumbled
turned around, the month abbreviation is read backwards
something captured is held inside its captor

blocks.note: the calendar abbreviation
the word that, letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Gossiping about an odd person caught at the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled word sits inside DEC written backwards, CED.
explanation.definitionFit: To chat is to talk informally, so having chatted is having talked.

clue.text: O my, is Sting another sexist?

indicators.note: another version of the letters means a different arrangement of them

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Shock that the rock singer Sting might be yet another chauvinist.
explanation.definitionFit: A misogynist hates or is prejudiced against women, the extreme kind of sexist.

clue.text: Like a pregnant fox, we follow a demon

blocks.note: a pregnant vixen is in cub
we gives us, placed after

explanation.surface: We trail behind an expectant vixen, which turns out to be an evil spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: An incubus is a male evil spirit of folklore said to visit sleepers.

clue.text: Money said to bring grief

indicators.note: said tells us the word is spoken, so we go by its sound

blocks.note: a dollar is a unit of money

explanation.surface: The old idea that money brings unhappiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolour is a literary word for sorrow or distress, a synonym of grief.

clue.text: A good distance? And not far from the truth

definitions.note: a hint at the idiom 'not by a long stretch', meaning far from it

blocks.note: first meaning: literally, by a large span
second meaning: the idiom, usually with not, about how far something is from true

explanation.surface: Measuring a long way, and then reassuring that something is nearly accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: The everyday idiom 'not by a long stretch' means not at all; the clue teases it with its own 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a long stretch is a great expanse; idiomatically the phrase measures degree, as in 'not by a long stretch'.

clue.text: Lump found in agency staff nurse

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits inside the words that follow
to nurse is to hold closely, so the two words cradle the answer within them

blocks.note: spans the end of agency and the start of staff

explanation.surface: A swelling discovered on a temporary nurse from an employment agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff nurse' reads as one job title, but nurse is a verb here, meaning hold.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is a sac of fluid under the skin that can be felt as a swelling.

clue.text: Logical to restrict little Alastair

blocks.note: to ration is to restrict supplies
Al is a short form of Alastair

explanation.surface: A sensible case for putting a small boy named Alastair on limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means based on reason and sound thinking, a synonym for logical.

clue.text: Food near, but dirty

blocks.note: grub is slang for food
by means near

explanation.surface: Food is close at hand but unappetisingly dirty.
explanation.definitionFit: Grubby means covered in grime, so it is a direct synonym for dirty.

clue.text: The Spanish do, twice, when artist enters the fabulous city

indicators.note: an artist who enters goes inside the doubled word

blocks.note: el is Spanish for the
the word do written two times
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A Spanish party held twice when a painter turns up in a legendary city.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, for Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist; 'do' here is a party, and the artist sits between its two copies.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the mythical city of gold sought by Spanish explorers in South America.

clue.text: Plane collection for those living in the fast lane

definitions.text: those living in the fast lane

blocks.note: a jet is a plane
a set is a collection

explanation.surface: A fleet of aircraft for high-flying people.
explanation.definitionFit: The jet set are wealthy socialites who travel widely and enjoy a glamorous lifestyle.
